### Observed differences

- The segment A19 → A20 ran in every trace in the earlier window (200 of 200 traces, with A19 before A20 in about 99 in 100 of them). In the later window it appears in only about 52 in 100 traces and is absent from about 48 in 100; when it does run, A19 still precedes A20. [OCC002, OCC003, REL010]

- The branch that followed shrank in step. Earlier, A25 and A26 ran together (A25 first) in about 50 in 100 traces and A27 alone in the other traces, the two options being mutually exclusive so that exactly one branch ran per trace. In the later window, A25/A26 run together in about 27 in 100 traces and A27 in about 26 in 100, essentially only alongside A19/A20, and in about 48 in 100 traces neither branch runs. [OCC004, OCC005, OCC006, REL011, REL013, REL025, REL026, REL031]

- The skip is visible directly at A43: earlier, about 96 in 100 of A43's observed outgoing transitions led to A19; in the later window they split between A19 (about 49 in 100) and A28 (about 46 in 100). The distance from A43 to A28 (in event steps, not clock time) was previously always 4–5 steps (about 46 in 100 at 4, 54 in 100 at 5) and is now a single step in about 48 in 100 cases. A28 itself still occurs in every trace in both windows, and its typical position barely moved (mean about 0.47 vs 0.44 of the trace), nor did A43's (about 0.34 vs 0.35). [DIR005, LAG003, REL014, REL021, POS002, POS003]

- Routing inside the executions that still contain the segment is essentially unchanged: A20 leads to A28 in about 99 in 100 of its outgoing transitions earlier and about 97 in 100 later, and A27 leads to A20 in about 99 vs 96 in 100. [DIR003, DIR004]

- A06 declined and shifted: it appears in about 32 in 100 traces earlier versus about 10 in 100 later; its median event position moved from near the end of the trace (about 0.97) to mid-trace (about 0.41); its outgoing transitions, previously dominated by A49 (about 85 in 100), are now spread, led by A47 (about 24 in 100) and A16 (about 19 in 100) with A49 down to about 5 in 100; and A48 now goes directly to A49 in about 97 in 100 of its transitions (about 71 in 100 earlier), the A48 → A06 edge having nearly disappeared. These figures rest on few later-window observations (about 19–21 traces or transitions; the A06–A49 step-distance comparison on only 6 pairs). [OCC001, POS001, DIR002, DIR007, LAG001, LAG004]

### Inference

Support level: Supported hypothesis

The evidence supports the hypothesis that, in the later window, the segment consisting of A19 → A20 together with the branch that followed it (either A25 → A26 or A27) is skipped in about half of the executions: earlier, every trace contained A19 → A20 followed by exactly one of the two branch options, whereas later about 48 in 100 traces contain none of these activities, and in those cases A43 leads directly to A28. Supporting signs: the participation drops are large (100% to about 52% for A19 and A20; about 50% to about 26% for each branch activity), the bypass is shown directly by A43's successor split and the collapsed A43–A28 distance, the preserved internal order and within-block routing indicate a bypass rather than a reordering or swap of activities, and the pattern is consistent across occurrence, relation, direction and lag indicators. Chance is also an unlikely explanation overall: 59 control-flow items qualified where about 0.85 would be expected for an unchanged process. A competing explanation the evidence cannot rule out is that the later window is a mixture containing a case variant that never executed this segment (for example a shorter case type) rather than the same cases having become able to skip it; the finite window sizes also limit precision. [OCC002, OCC003, OCC004, OCC005, OCC006, REL010, REL014, REL026, DIR005, LAG003]

Other differences: A06 declined (about 32 in 100 traces to about 10 in 100), moved from the end to the middle of traces, and its successors changed from mostly A49 to a spread led by A47 and A16, with A48 → A49 now almost always immediate; this may be a side effect of the same restructuring or a separate difference, and with only about 19–21 later-window observations behind it the evidence cannot distinguish these. A04's outgoing transitions also changed completely, but only 11 were observed per window, so this carries little weight. [OCC001, POS001, DIR002, DIR007, LAG001, LAG004, REL001, REL006, DIR001]

Let me analyse this evidence carefully.

Screening: 170 units tested, 59 items qualified, 0.85 expected without change. 59 items is many times larger than 0.85, so the count cannot be explained by chance. All items are control_flow family. So we move past the screening comparison and judge by directness, consistency, and ability to rule out competing explanations.

Now let me understand the behavioural picture.

Key observations:

1. OCC001 (A06): participation dropped from 0.315 (about 63 in 200 traces) to 0.095 (about 19 in 200). Mean occurrences per trace 0.34 → 0.105. Decreased.

2. OCC002 (A19): participation 1.0 → 0.515. Mean occurrences 1.005 → 0.525. So A19 was in every trace before, now in about half.

3. OCC003 (A20): participation 1.0 → 0.515. Same pattern.

4. OCC004 (A25): participation 0.505 → 0.265.

5. OCC005 (A26): participation 0.51 → 0.275.

6. OCC006 (A27): participation 0.50 → 0.255.

So A19, A20 were mandatory (100% participation) before and became optional (~50%) after. A25, A26, A27 were ~50% before and ~25-27% after. A06 was ~31.5% before and ~9.5% after.

7. REL010 (A19, A20): before cooccurrence 1.0, A_before_B 0.995 (A19 before A20 in essentially all traces). After: cooccurrence 0.515, neither 0.485, A_before_B 0.5. So the pair A19→A20 executed together in all traces before; after, in about half the traces they don't co-occur at all, and when they do, A19 still precedes A20.

8. REL014 (A19, A28): before cooccurrence 1.0, A19 before A28 0.99. After: cooccurrence 0.515, B_only (A28 only) 0.485, A_before_B 0.505. So A28 still always occurs, but in half the traces A19 is absent.

9. REL015 (A19, A43): before cooccurrence 1.0, B_before_A 0.99 (A43 before A19). After: cooccurrence 0.515, B_only 0.485, B_before_A 0.505. Same pattern.

10. REL021 (A20, A28): before cooccurrence 1.0, A20 before A28 0.995. After: cooccurrence 0.515, B_only 0.485, A_before_B 0.51.

11. REL022 (A20, A43): before cooccurrence 1.0, A43 before A20 0.995. After: cooccurrence 0.515, B_only 0.485, B_before_A 0.51.

12. REL024 (A20, A49): before cooccurrence 1.0, A20 before A49 1.0. After: cooccurrence 0.515, B_only 0.485, A_before_B 0.51.

So the pattern: A19 and A20 always occurred (in sequence A19 then A20) in the before window; in the after window, they occur together in about half the traces and are both absent in the other half (REL010: neither 0.485). Meanwhile A28, A43, A48, A49 still occur in all traces. So the block A19→A20 became optional/skipped in about half the traces.

13. REL011 (A19, A25): before cooccurrence 0.505, A_only 0.495, A_before_B 0.495. After: cooccurrence 0.265, A_only 0.25, neither 0.485. So before, A19 always present; A25 present in half; when A25 present, A19 before it. After, both absent in ~48.5%.

14. REL018 (A20, A25): before cooccurrence 0.505, A_only 0.495, B_before_A 0.505 (A25 before A20). After: cooccurrence 0.265, neither 0.485.

15. REL026 (A25, A27): before A_only 0.5, B_only 0.495 (mutually exclusive alternatives), after A_only 0.265, B_only 0.255, neither 0.48. So A25 and A27 were alternatives (one or the other in every trace); after, in ~48% of traces neither occurs.

16. REL031 (A26, A27): before A_only 0.5, B_only 0.49, after A_only 0.265, B_only 0.245, neither 0.48. Same: alternatives became both absent in half the traces.

17. REL003-REL005 (A06 with A25/A26/A27): before, cooccurrence ~0.15-0.165, neither ~0.335-0.345; after, neither ~0.665-0.675. A06 participation dropped.

18. REL001/REL002 (A06 with A19/A20): before cooccurrence 0.315, B_only 0.685 (A19/A20 always present, A06 sometimes); after cooccurrence 0.05, B_only 0.465, neither 0.44. So A06 co-occurred with A19/A20 in ~31.5% before; after, in 5%, and in 44% neither.

19. DIR002 (A06): before, outgoing transitions dominated by A49 (0.85); after, spread over many activities with A47 0.238, A16 0.19, A28 0.095. Support before 67, after 21. A06's outgoing profile changed completely. But support is small (21 outgoing transitions after). This is consistent with A06 now occurring in different contexts (earlier position — POS001 shows A06's mean position moved from ~0.89 to ~0.52 of the trace).

20. POS001 (A06): mean position 0.89 → 0.52, median 0.97 → 0.41. So A06 moved from near the end of traces to mid-trace. But support dropped from 63 to 19 events. Position is relative position in trace. Hmm, this could reflect that A06 now occurs in the shorter traces (without the A19/A20 tail?). Actually if A19/A20 block is skipped, traces get shorter, and A06's relative position changes.

Wait — actually, let me think about what the underlying change might be. Before: every trace has A19 → A20 (participation 1.0 each, A19 before A20 0.995). A25/A26/A27 each ~50%, mutually exclusive-ish (A25 vs A27 alternatives; A26 vs A27 alternatives; A25 & A26 co-occur 0.5 — REL025 shows A25 before A26 cooccurrence 0.5, so A25 and A26 both occur in half the traces, A25 before A26). Hmm wait, REL025 (A25, A26): before cooccurrence 0.5, A_before_B 0.5, neither 0.485. So in half the traces both A25 and A26 occur (A25 then A26), in the other half neither? But A25 participation is 0.505 and A26 is 0.51, and A26 vs A27 (REL031): A_only 0.5, B_only 0.49 — so A26 and A27 never co-occur; one of them always present. And A25 vs A27 (REL026): A_only 0.5, B_only 0.495 — never co-occur. So structure before: A25 → A26 in ~50% of traces, A27 in ~50% of traces. These are two alternative branches.

After: A25 ~26.5%, A26 ~27.5%, A27 ~25.5%, and neither-of-A25/A27 in ~48% (REL026), neither-of-A26/A27 in 48% (REL031). And A19/A20 in ~51.5%. Hmm, REL011 (A19, A25): after cooccurrence 0.265, neither 0.485. So when A19/A20 present (~51.5%), A25/A26 present (~26.5%)? And A27 cooccurrence with A19 after: REL013 (A19, A27): after cooccurrence 0.25, neither 0.48. Hmm, so A25 and A27 both co-occur with A19 about equally after? Before, REL013: cooccurrence 0.5, A_only 0.5 — A19 always, A27 in half.

Hmm, this is getting complex. Let me simplify: the dominant, consistent story is:

- The block A19 → A20, which was executed in every trace before (participation 100%, A19 immediately/always before A20), is executed in only about half the traces after and skipped in the other half (neither 48.5%). This is a change: an activity pair became optional — part of the process is skipped in ~half the cases.

- Consequently, A25/A26/A27, which appeared in ~50% of traces before, now appear in ~25% each. A25 and A26 still run together (REL025 after: cooccurrence 0.265, neither 0.725); A27 alone. Before, exactly one of {A25→A26 branch, A27} per trace; after, these branches run in ~25% each and in ~48% of traces neither runs.

Wait, but is it that the branches became optional too, or is it that the whole segment became optional? Let's check: after, A19/A20 present 51.5%, neither 48.5%. A25 present 26.5%, A27 present 25.5%, and REL026 after: A_only 0.265, B_only 0.255, neither 0.48. So in the after window, in ~51% of traces either A25/A26 or A27 runs, and in ~48% neither. And A19/A20 in ~51.5%. Do A25/A26 co-occur with A19 after? REL011: cooccurrence 0.265, A_only (A19 only) 0.25, neither 0.485. So A25 occurs only when A19 occurs (A25 ⊂ A19 traces roughly: A25 0.265 ≈ cooccurrence 0.265, A_only 0.25 means A19 without A25 in 25%). Similarly REL013 (A19, A27): after cooccurrence 0.25, A_only 0.265, neither 0.48. So A27 occurs only when A19 occurs.

So after: ~51.5% of traces have the A19→A20 block; within those, half have A25→A26 and half have A27. The other ~48.5% have neither A19/A20 nor A25/A26/A27. Before: 100% had A19→A20; within those, half had A25→A26, half had A27.

So the change: the entire block (A19 → A20 followed by branch A25→A26 or A27) became optional — skipped in about half of the traces. Alternatively: a new path bypassing this block was introduced / the block became skippable.

Also A06: participation 31.5% → 9.5%, position moved from end (~0.89-0.97) to middle (~0.52), and its successor profile changed completely (DIR002: before mostly A49 85%, after spread with A47 24%, A16 19%). Support for DIR002 after is only 21 outgoing transitions — weak. POS001 support after is 19 events. These are low-support items. A06's behaviour changed but with few observations.

Hmm, wait. Let me reconsider. Maybe A06 relates to the skipped block. Before: A06 in 31.5% of traces, near the end (position ~0.9), mostly followed by A49. After: A06 in 9.5%, mid-position, varied successors. REL001 (A06, A19): before cooccurrence 0.315, B_only 0.685, B_before_A 0.28 — so when A06 occurs, it's after A19 (A19 before A06 in 0.28 of traces, cooccurrence 0.315, A_before_B 0.01). So A06 came after the A19/A20 block before. After: cooccurrence 0.05, A_only 0.045, B_only 0.465, neither 0.44. So A06 now mostly occurs without A19/A20 (A_only 0.045 vs cooccurrence 0.05 — roughly split). Hmm, A06 participation after is 0.095 = 0.045 + 0.05. So A06 occurs half the time without the A19/A20 block.

LAG001 (A06, A49): before, A49 follows A06 within 1 step in 100% of the 57 supported cases; after, lag 3 in 83%, lag 1 in 17% (support after only 6 — very weak). So A06 → A49 direct succession mostly gone; now 3 steps apart. Weak support (6 observations).

LAG003 (A43, A28): before, A43 followed by A28 at lag 4-5 (46%/54%); after, lag 1 in 48%, lag 2 in 2.6%, lag 4 24%, lag 5 25%. Support ~196/193 — strong. So the distance between A43 and A28 shrank: previously A28 came 4-5 events after A43; now typically immediately after (lag 1). This suggests the block between A43 and A28 (which would include A19→A20 and the branch?) was removed/skipped, so A28 now directly follows A43.

Let me check ordering: REL015 (A19, A43): before B_before_A 0.99 — A43 before A19. REL022 (A20, A43): before B_before_A 0.995 — A43 before A20. So order before: A43 ... A19 → A20 ... A28? And LAG003: A43 then A28 at lag 4-5. So between A43 and A28 there were ~4-5 events: A19, A20, and branch activities (A25/A26 or A27 — that's 1-2 more). A43, A19, A20, A25, A26, A28? That's lag 5 from A43 to A28 (positions A43=0, A19=1, A20=2, A25=3, A26=4, A28=5). Or with A27: A43, A19, A20, A27, A28 — lag 4. That matches lag 4/5 split (46% lag 4 = A27 branch, 54% lag 5 = A25/A26 branch — and branch frequencies were ~50/50!). 

After: A28 follows A43 at lag 1 in 48% — direct. In the other traces (24% lag 4, 25% lag 5), the block still runs. 48% ≈ the share where the block is skipped. Beautifully consistent: the block A19→A20 + branch (A25/A26 or A27) between A43 and A28 is skipped in ~half the traces, so A28 directly follows A43.

Also DIR005 (A43): before, A43 → A19 96%; after, A43 → A19 49%, A43 → A28 46%. So before, A43 was almost always followed by A19; after, A43 is followed by A28 directly in 46% (the skip cases) and by A19 in 49% (the non-skip cases). This directly confirms: the successor of A43 changed from A19 to (A19 or A28). Strong support with 201/200 outgoing transitions.

DIR007 (A48): before A48 → A49 71%, A48 → A06 28%; after A48 → A49 97%. So A48 now almost always goes to A49; the A48→A06 edge nearly disappeared (A06 participation dropped). Consistent with A06's decline.

DIR003 (A20): before A20 → A28 99.5%; after A20 → A28 97%. Stable. DIR004 (A27): before A27 → A20 99%; after A27 → A20 96%. Stable. So within the block, routing unchanged.

LAG004 (A48, A49): lag 1 71% → 97%. So A48→A49 became immediate. Before, 29% had something between A48 and A49 — probably A06 (A48 → A06 → A49, since DIR007 before had A48→A06 28%). After, A06 rarely occurs, so A48→A49 direct in 97%. Consistent.

LAG002 (A26, A28): lag 2 before and after (96% lag 2 after). Stable-ish, small change. Support 100/53.

POS002 (A28): mean position 0.467 → 0.437, small shift. POS003 (A43): 0.336 → 0.352, small shift. These are minor.

So the coherent main hypothesis: In the later window, the sub-block consisting of A19 → A20 together with the alternative branch (A25 → A26 or A27) that used to run in every case between A43 and A28 is skipped in about half of the executions; A28 now directly follows A43 in those cases. I.e., a block of activities became optional / a bypass path emerged.

Wait — but the instructions warn: "A change in how often existing paths are taken requires that every activity and path involved is observed in a substantial share of traces in both windows, and that only the shares between alternatives shift; it is not a replacement of one path by another. It does not apply when an activity or path is (nearly) absent in one window, when a predecessor now leads directly to a successor so that a group of activities is bypassed..."

Here, the predecessor A43 now leads directly to A28 (DIR005: A43→A28 46% after, 0 before... wait, before A43→A28 was not in the profile; before A43→A19 96%). So this is the "bypass" case: a group of activities (A19, A20, A25/A26/A27) is bypassed. So the hypothesis is "part of the process is skipped" — activities became optional / a block is bypassed. That's supported by participation drops + DIR successor change + LAG change.

The hypothesis: the block A19 → A20 (with the alternative sub-branches A25→A26 or A27) became skippable: before it ran in 100% of traces; after it runs in ~51% and is bypassed in ~49%, with A43 leading directly to A28 in the bypass cases.

Supporting evidence:
- OCC002/OCC003: A19, A20 participation 100% → ~51%.
- OCC004-006: A25, A26, A27 participation ~50% → ~25%.
- REL010: A19 & A20 co-occur 100% → 51.5%, neither 48.5%; order A19 before A20 preserved when present.
- REL014/021: A28 still always present; A19/A20 co-occur with it only ~51%.
- DIR005: A43's dominant successor changed from A19 (96%) to split A19 (49%) / A28 (46%).
- LAG003: A43→A28 distance collapsed from 4-5 steps to 1 step in ~48% of cases.
- REL011/013/018/020: branch activities now co-occur with A19/A20 and are absent together with them.
- REL026/031: A25/A27 and A26/A27 were mutually exclusive alternatives before (one always present); after both absent in ~48%.

Competing explanations: Could this be a sampling fluctuation? No — screening says 59 items vs 0.85 expected; the count is ~70x the chance expectation. Could it be that the after window mixes two variants where one lacks the block? That's essentially what "block became optional" means. Could A06's change be a separate change? A06: participation 31.5% → 9.5%, position moved, successors changed. DIR002 support is 11/11 outgoing transitions — very weak. POS001 support 63/19 events. LAG001 support 57/6 — very weak. So A06's changes rest on few observations. A06 seems related: before, A06 occurred after the block near the end (A48 → A06 → A49 in ~28%); after, A06 rarely occurs. This could be part of the same restructuring (the path through A06 shrank) or a separate difference. I'll report it under other differences.

Now, support level: The screening comparison: 59 items vs 0.85 expected — many times larger, so we proceed. The hypothesis is direct (DIR005 shows the successor change directly; LAG003 shows the bypass directly; OCC/REL show the participation change), consistent (many items align), and competing explanations (chance) are ruled out by the screening count and by coherence. I'd say "Supported hypothesis".

Is it "a group of activities is bypassed" — the instruction says the "shift in path frequencies" hypothesis doesn't apply here; instead this indicates activities became optional/skipped. That's fine — the hypothesis is "part of the process is executed less often / skipped", which is listed as supportable: "Changes in participation, routing shares or repetition can support a hypothesis that part of the process is executed more often, less often, skipped or repeated differently".

So: Supported hypothesis: In the later window, the sequence A19 → A20 and the alternative branch activities A25/A26 and A27 that followed it are skipped in about half of the cases; A43 now leads directly to A28 in those cases. Before, A19 → A20 ran in every trace (A43 → A19 in 96% of A43's outgoing transitions), and exactly one of the two branches (A25 → A26, or A27) ran in each trace. After, A19 and A20 appear in ~51% of traces (down from 100%), A25/A26/A27 in ~25% each (down from ~50%), and in ~48% of traces none of them appears, with A28 immediately following A43 (lag 1 in ~48% of cases, up from 0; previously lag 4-5).

Limitations: we cannot tell from these windows whether a new bypass edge was added or whether the block became optional via a skip construct; also the A06 changes rest on few observations. Also, the windows are finite samples.

Also A48 → A49 became immediate (lag 1: 71% → 97%), consistent with A06's decline (A48→A06 share fell from ~28% to ~0.5%).

Hmm, should A06 be part of the main hypothesis? The main hypothesis is about the A19/A20 block being skipped. A06's decline is arguably a separate difference (or a consequence). The instruction: "If the evidence also shows other differences that are not part of this hypothesis, report them afterwards under 'Other differences:'". A06's change is not part of the block-skip hypothesis per se — it's a participation/position change of a different activity. I'll report it under Other differences.

Now, evidence citation rules: every bullet/paragraph stating a fact about the data or hypothesis must end with exactly one pair of square brackets listing supporting evidence identifiers. Name at most three resource codes — no resource items here, so N/A. No TWAIT items, so don't discuss elapsed times. POS/LAG use event positions — I should note that LAG is in event steps, not clock time.

Let me now check numbers to present:

- A19: participation 100% → 51.5% (about 200/200 → about 103/200). Mean occurrences 1.005 → 0.525.
- A20: 100% → 51.5%.
- A25: 50.5% → 26.5%. A26: 51% → 27.5%. A27: 50% → 25.5%.
- A06: 31.5% → 9.5%.
